messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: coordinating release of 1.0.1
parts:
We're ready to go on the Stan side for 1.0.1.
So the issue is how we freeze the Stan code,
let Jiqiang work on RStan until it's ready to
go, then push a release.

Jiqiang -- what exactly do you work from in
RStan?

What we're worried about is changes to Stan
while Jiqiang's working on RStan.

This is definitely related to Ben's notes on
release management. If we want to synch releases
of Stan and RStan and tag them, then they have
to be ready to go at the same time.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] coordinating release of 1.0.1
parts:
We can release rstan as what it is now as 1.0.1.  

I am working on an issue (a segfault) I can somehow reproduce but not able to figure out the exact reason.  But we can release another version of RStan later if I cannot figure it soon. 

I think we need to work out a way to release RStan without releasing Stan as Ben had pointed out there are 
cases when there is bug in RStan.  But I can see the issue is that when it is time to release another version of RStan, Stan gets updated as well.  

Jiqiang

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: coordinating release of 1.0.1
parts:
Just to say I have patched rstan somehow that I do not have the problem described below though I have not figure out what is the real reason for one issue.  So I think I am ready for the release. 

There are two problems. 

1. weird segfault I talked before. It is not a problem with the memory on my computer.  It is just because if the dynamic shared object is released by R's garbage collector earlier than the c++ object that is exposed by Rcpp, we would have segfault when R is releasing the c++ object (but the compiled code is gone).  Normally this would happen since the dynamic object is unloaded later.  

2. previously it seems that compiling two different stan model is problematic as the later will overwrite the first one.  I have not figure out why.  But now I use different Rcpp module names for different models, which seems to be able to _control_ the problem. 


--
Jiqiang
